content:
This interesting project developed by Jeff Halter (introduced by Daring Fireball) allows users to run classic 68k After Dark screensaver modules on modern Macs. Details below.

「在現代 macOS 上運行經典 After Dark 螢幕保護程式」

Depending on how long you've been using or interested in Macs, you may remember After Dark—a collection of screensavers that were practically a staple of Macintosh computers in the 1990s. At the very least, you may have some recollection of the famous Flying Toasters screensaver.

Over the years, running these classic screensavers has typically required old hardware or classic Mac OS emulators, but the latter is often unreliable. However, a new project called Afterglow makes the process much simpler on modern Macs.

As John Gruber noted on Daring Fireball, the project was developed by Jeff Halter, who previously created Lunacy—a native Swift app that lets users play the classic game Lunatic Fringe from More After Dark on modern Macs.

Afterglow uses an emulator specifically designed for After Dark modules to run the original programs, without requiring a full classic Mac OS environment. Notably, Afterglow also includes a built-in modern macOS screensaver module, allowing users to set any imported After Dark module as their Mac's screensaver.

Here's Halter on the philosophy behind the project:

In the 90s, Berkeley Systems' After Dark screensavers brought Flying Toasters, Fish, and Starry Skylines to every Macintosh screen. These programs served a practical purpose in preventing burn-in on CRT displays, while also being entertaining—the animations were fun, surreal, beautiful, and sometimes even nauseating. These are works of art worth preserving. Running After Dark modules today often involves complicated Mac OS emulator setups or old hardware. Still, no single emulator or old computer can run every module perfectly: sometimes the animations are too fast, sometimes too slow. Afterglow is an emulator designed specifically for running After Dark modules—it runs the original 68k module code, not remade or ported versions—and doesn't require ROMs or classic Mac OS. In the spirit of software preservation, it lets people easily enjoy After Dark, both today and for years to come.

The project's website notes that Afterglow itself doesn't ship with After Dark modules, but provides tutorials on finding and importing them.

Halter also mentions that Afterglow includes a variety of built-in features, including module control, fullscreen mode, random playback, multi-module support, 3D cover flow, CRT shaders, a resource viewer, and the DrawMorph editor.
